section_summary: This section chiefly documents military and theater clearances for traders, private travelers, and refugees seeking entry into occupied Japan, including questions about extensions, nationality, documentation, and reentry rights. It also records the inauguration of organized tourism and includes a detailed SCAP guide covering customs, currency, communications, legal restrictions, medical care, and practical needs. The final pages concern refugees traveling from Dairen and follow-up cases involving D. Koppius, Bernard Rogard/Hisami Ahtem, and T. P. Berman.

subfiles.title: Return of military permit no. 6171 for Victor Kelley Bashi
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Returns Bashi's unused military permit after notifying the Bangkok embassy of his theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: Chappell returns military permit 6171, issued August 16 for Victor Kelley Bashi, and notes that Bangkok was notified.

subfiles.title: Instructions for a renewed permit application for Victor Kelley Bashi
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Explains how Bashi's firm should seek a replacement military permit.
subfiles.summary: The Department directs Bashi's firm to reapply through the Commerce Department's New York office and return his unused permit.

subfiles.title: File charge-out card for 18.00/7-1945
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a file item.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out card for file 18.00/7-1945, dated October 13, 1958.

subfiles.title: File charge-out card
subfiles.about: Records an unidentified file charge.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out card bearing the notation 11/10/57.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning Jakob Szpiro's clearance
subfiles.to: Department of State, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Requests confirmation and cable notification of Jakob Szpiro's final SCAP approval.
subfiles.summary: Globex asks whether Szpiro's Commerce-approved application received SCAP approval and requests notification to the Shanghai consulate.

subfiles.title: Entry clearance telegram for T. P. Berman
subfiles.about: Authorizes Berman's entry into Japan for a sixty-day business visit.
subfiles.summary: Berman may enter between July 15 and August 15, carrying photographs and certified clearance instructions.

subfiles.title: Universal Peltry Traders application for T. P. Berman
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Applies for Berman to purchase furs and arrange future business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The application identifies Berman as a Russian émigré purchasing agent in Tientsin and proposes a one-to-two-month Japanese visit.

subfiles.title: Entry clearance telegram for Nefeh J. Sbath
subfiles.about: Authorizes Nefeh J. Sbath to enter Japan for sixty days.
subfiles.summary: The Syrian representative may enter July 15–August 15 and must carry photographs and the prescribed statement or telegram copy.

subfiles.title: Entry clearance telegram for D. Koppius
subfiles.about: Authorizes D. Koppius to enter Japan for sixty days.
subfiles.summary: The Dutch representative may enter July 15–August 15 with photographs and the required statement or certified telegram text.

subfiles.title: Extension clearance for D. Koppius
subfiles.about: Grants Koppius a September extension and requests agency notification.
subfiles.summary: Koppius's original July permit is extended to September 1–30, 1948, under its existing conditions.

subfiles.title: Japan travel permit extensions and cancellations
subfiles.from: Michael Lee, Office of International Trade
subfiles.to: Major E. Larson, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Requests revised entry periods for six Japan travel applicants.
subfiles.summary: Commerce requests extensions for D. Koppius, Joseph Liberman, Francis Ogmea, Masao Shinkai, Adelph Shefte, and Dan Brechner.

subfiles.title: American Pacific Enterprises application for D. Koppius
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Applies for Koppius to visit Japan on company business.
subfiles.summary: The application identifies Koppius as Dutch and based in Shanghai, requesting sixty days to visit Osaka, Tokyo, and Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Military clearance for John M. Bowes
subfiles.about: Reports Bowes's clearance for entry during August 1948.
subfiles.summary: John M. Bowes of Manila is cleared for sixty days, with entry permitted August 1–31.

subfiles.title: Entry clearance telegram for John M. Bowes
subfiles.about: Notifies Manila of Bowes's military clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bowes may enter August 1–31 for sixty days and should receive certified instructions in lieu of the required statement.

subfiles.title: Report on Maji Tacla and family
subfiles.from: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Reports the Tacla family's departure from Japan after receiving transit visas.
subfiles.summary: The Tacla family left Haneda for the United States and was presumed subsequently documented by Brazil's consul general in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Brazil concerning the Tacla family
subfiles.about: Relays Yokohama's report on the Tacla family's departure.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports that the family left Haneda for the United States after receiving Yokohama transit visas.

subfiles.title: Request for additional information concerning Harry Julius Hurwitz
subfiles.to: Legation of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Requests details of the goods Hurwitz intends to trade in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Army requires information about the goods Hurwitz wishes to buy, sell, or investigate before submitting his application to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Army request for information on Harry Julius Hurwitz
subfiles.from: W. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Seeks commercial details needed to submit Hurwitz's application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Scott asks what goods Hurwitz intends to buy, sell, or investigate.

subfiles.title: Entry clearance for George Victor de Villiers
subfiles.about: Notifies de Villiers of his Japanese entry clearance while excluding his wife.
subfiles.summary: De Villiers may enter during August for sixty days; his wife was not cleared.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 445 on Japanese tourist trade
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Reports approval of seven-day package tours and encloses a tourist guide.
subfiles.summary: SCAP approved organized tours, and Sebald forwarded twelve copies of its new information guide for tourists.

subfiles.title: Information for Tourists Coming to Japan
subfiles.about: Explains the rules and practical arrangements governing organized tourism in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: The guide restricts tourists to scheduled Japan Travel Bureau itineraries and explains customs, identification, currency exchange, mail, telephones, and telegraphs. It outlines applicable Japanese and occupation law, military-police authority, and export limits. Medical charges, hospitals, immunization, clothing, and scarce personal supplies are also covered.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Tokyo's clearance telegram to Dairen
subfiles.about: Forwards the text of Tokyo's July 16 clearance message.
subfiles.summary: The Department orders transmission of Tokyo's unnumbered July 16 telegram to the Dairen consulate.

subfiles.title: SCAP clearance for three women traveling from Dairen
subfiles.to: American Consul, Dairen; Department of State informed
subfiles.about: Clears three named women to enter Japan aboard a repatriation vessel.
subfiles.summary: SCAP grants entry clearance to Ne Jiya, Aniss U. Wbgeii, and Mahtserwar Yungurazi and permits repatriation-vessel travel.

subfiles.title: Conditional clearances for Dairen refugees
subfiles.about: Reports unconditional and conditional permissions for refugees from Dairen to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Several refugees receive clearance; Greek applicants must prove citizenship and funds, while others must document Chinese status. No assurance of permanent Japanese residence is given.

subfiles.title: Theater clearance for Bernard Rogard or Hisami Ahtem
subfiles.from: W. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Reports theater clearance for a stateless traveler currently in Tientsin.
subfiles.summary: The consul may validate Rogard or Ahtem's passport for sixty days if he holds Chinese reentry clearance.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on the Rogard-Ahtem application
subfiles.about: Records that the application originated in the theater rather than State or Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Army confirmed that Tokyo's clearance supplied no authorized entry dates.

subfiles.title: Entry clearance telegram for Bernard Rogard or Hisami Ahtem
subfiles.about: Authorizes Rogard or Ahtem to enter Japan subject to Chinese reentry clearance.
subfiles.summary: The stateless traveler may stay sixty days and must carry photographs and possess permission to reenter China.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for file 894.111/7-1848
subfiles.about: Records an internal charge of the Koppius file.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for file 894.111/7-1848 and a Commerce letter copy.

subfiles.title: Internal paper-routing slip
subfiles.about: Routes a requested file paper internally.
subfiles.summary: Partially legible routing slip for a requested paper.

subfiles.title: Conversation with American Pacific Enterprises about D. Koppius
subfiles.from: L. S. Mellor, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records company authorization to cable Koppius's September clearance to Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Lasley confirmed Koppius remained in Shanghai and authorized State to notify him of his September 1948 theater clearance.

subfiles.title: September entry clearance telegram for D. Koppius
subfiles.about: Notifies Koppius of his extended permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Koppius may enter during September and remain sixty days, with documentation under earlier instructions.

subfiles.title: Nationality warning concerning T. P. Berman
subfiles.about: Warns that Berman's clearance may be revoked if he carries a Soviet passport.
subfiles.summary: The consul should notify Tokyo if Berman departs and may warn him that Japan could review his status upon arrival.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about T. P. Berman's Soviet citizenship
subfiles.about: Asks whether Berman's entry permission remains valid after discovering Soviet citizenship.
subfiles.summary: Tientsin reports that Berman is a Soviet citizen, not a Russian émigré, and requests guidance.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Anatole Muroff about T. P. Berman
subfiles.from: H. Corkran, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records Muroff's explanation of Berman's nationality and residence history.
subfiles.summary: Muroff said Berman had lived in China for thirty years, lacked a Soviet passport, and was Soviet only under Soviet law.
